title: Event-Driven Microservices with Kafka & Faust (PYTH_174_S1 to PYTH_174_S8)

slides.title: Stream Processing with Faust
slides.prompt: Faust brings Kafka stream processing concepts to Python, using AsyncIO for high-throughput event processing.
slides.codeSnippet:
import faust

app = faust.App('order-app', broker='kafka://localhost:9092')
topic = app.topic('orders', value_type=Order)

slides.title: Defining Faust Stream Agents
slides.prompt: Fill in the Faust decorator used to create a stream processing agent that consumes Kafka messages.

slides.title: Kafka Consumer Groups
slides.prompt: How do Kafka Consumer Groups enable horizontal scaling across multiple Python instances?
options: By assigning distinct topic partitions exclusively to individual worker instances within the group
By broadcasting all messages to every consumer simultaneously
By caching event payloads inside a shared Redis memory cluster
By executing round-robin load balancing on incoming REST API calls
slides.correctAnswer: By assigning distinct topic partitions exclusively to individual worker instances within the group

slides.title: Event Record Modeling
slides.prompt: Fill in the Faust base class used to declare typed message schemas for Kafka topics.

slides.title: Eventual Consistency in EDAs
slides.prompt: What design strategy guarantees eventual consistency across microservices in an event-driven architecture?
options: Saga Pattern using compensating transactions on failure events
Two-Phase Commit (2PC) over raw HTTP REST calls
slides.correctAnswer: Saga Pattern using compensating transactions on failure events

slides.title: Kafka Topic Partition Keys
slides.prompt: Fill in the event parameter used by Kafka to guarantee order of related messages in the same partition.

slides.title: At-Least-Once Delivery Guarantees
slides.prompt: Why must stream consumers be idempotent when handling event streams with at-least-once semantics?
options: Because network retries can cause duplicate delivery of identical event messages
To force consumers to compress event streams using gzip
To speed up disk write operations on Kafka brokers
To convert incoming JSON payloads into binary Protobuf files
slides.correctAnswer: Because network retries can cause duplicate delivery of identical event messages

slides.title: Faust State Tables
slides.prompt: Fill in the persistent state management feature built into Faust for streaming aggregations.
